In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new, efficient and inexpensive method for the synthesis of FGF-1, a growth factor that is involved in the proliferation of cells and the healing of wounds, and which is used in the treatment of diabetic ulcers, chronic wounds and burns.
the development of a novel, nonviral gene therapy approach for treating the most common form of heart failure, dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).
the development of a novel, efficient, and safe strategy to deliver FGF-1 into the central nervous system of a rodent animal model of Parkinson’s disease (PD) using a viral vector system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the T7 system for the expression of recombinant proteins has become a very common and widely used method in molecular and cellular biology.
the FGF-1 protein has the potential to be an effective therapeutic agent for a wide array of conditions.
the FGF family is a large and complex family of growth factors with diverse roles in embryonic development and in the maintenance of adult tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the FGF1 gene (Gln64Arg) can affect the biological activity of the encoded protein (FGF-1), and that the SNP is associated with a number of diseases.
we were able to show that the T7 expression system is capable of producing recombinant human FGF-1 with proper physico-chemical and biological properties in a high yield and purity.
we have successfully demonstrated that the SHuffle T7 system is capable of producing a recombinant human growth factor with proper physicochemcial and biological properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SHuffle T7 system is a very useful tool for producing recombinant proteins in E. coli.
the SHuffle™ strain is a great platform strain for high-level production of recombinant proteins, especially those containing disulfide bonds.
